failures.criterion: 3a / the spec's Outcome - a denied issue-topic publish is named and counted instead of retried silently. It still is not, when one publish window sends the same subject twice. Two comments a person writes a moment apart share an owner topic and one batch publishes both through one window: one send is answered its denial, the other is reported as "NATS is unreachable", its event released with no attempt counted, the counter recording reason="failed", no line naming the subject, and the rest of that scan's backlog abandoned. INFRA-749's alert does not fire for that event.
failures.evidence:
Cause: the record this round adds holds one violation per subject (packages/envoy/internal/bus/nats.go:299-307, map[string]publishViolation) and a read takes it out (denials.go:87-96, delete then return), while recordPublishDenial overwrites the entry a second refusal of the same subject earns (denials.go:72). nats-server reports one violation per refused message, so a window that sent the subject twice earns two violations and the record can answer only one. The other send falls through window.acknowledged's denial arm to bus.ErrUnavailable (async.go:253-256), which settle releases the event on (outbox/publisher.go:383-386) before `default: backOff`, and publishBatch then marks the batch unavailable (publisher.go:306-310). The contract the bus owes is one violation per refused message, not one per subject.

Red test: TestRunCountsADeniedSubjectOncePerRefusedMessage, packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox/core_denied_test.go, commit f1edd351c454. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/outbox/ -run TestRunCountsADeniedSubjectOncePerRefusedMessage -count=3.   core_denied_test.go:477: line "level=INFO msg=\"dispatch outbox: event released\" event_id=1 error=\"publish owner topic \\\"notifications.dispatch.issue.T-1.comment.created\\\": bus: NATS is unreachable: nats: timeout waiting for ack\"" reports a denied publish as an outage of the bus
The two events differ from the test above it only in publishing one subject twice: both are a session's comment on one issue, so neither notifies and each has its owner topic alone. The rest of the package is green at the same commit (go test ./internal/dispatch/outbox/ -count=1: only this test fails, 184 s).

Same failure on the real surface, no test rig: on the stack at 127.0.0.1:8855 described above, three further comments posted on the same issue in quick succession leave attempt_count uneven at 10, 3, 1 and 2 across the four comment events, /metrics gains reason="failed" 14 beside reason="denied" 64, and the process log holds
  level=INFO msg="dispatch outbox: event released" event_id=5 error="publish owner topic \"notifications.dispatch.issue.R2-1.comment.created\": bus: NATS is unreachable: nats: timeout waiting for ack ..."
  level=ERROR msg="dispatch outbox: NATS is unreachable, so the batch from this event on waits for the next scan" event_id=5
beside, in the same pass, an event_id=7 line that names both of its destinations as denials. Before those three comments the same process had no reason="failed" series at all.

Achievable: the server reports one violation per refused message, so a record that keeps them per subject in the order they arrived - and hands each send the one that answers it - closes the class rather than this instance. The design is the implementer's; the test pins the observable contract.

notFindings: The per-subject record is bounded: recordPublishDenial drops every entry older than publishDenialRetention each time it records one, and a read takes its entry out, so a connection refused publishes to ever new subjects cannot grow it without bound.

The sentAt guard is correct for the case it was written for: a violation recorded before this publish put its message on the wire belongs to an earlier publish of the subject and is not read as this one's. The resend after ErrNotStored takes its own send time.
A reconnect and a replacement connection both clear the record (recovery.go:51-54, nats.go:496-499), so a violation of the previous session never answers a publish on the new one.
The regular expression that reads a refused subject matches nats-server's %q and unquotes it, so a subject holding a quote or a backslash is recorded under the name the publisher sent.
The core publish path still reads the connection's last error (confirmPublished), which is sound there because sendCore republishes each unconfirmed send alone on the connection.
forArchitect: The round fails on one entry. Round 1's two findings are both closed and proven closed by mutations of my own, and the change is correct for a window that sends each denied subject once. It is not correct when one window sends the same subject twice, which two comments on one issue in quick succession produce: the record holds one violation per subject and a read takes it, so the second send is reported as an unreachable bus, its event released with no attempt counted and the backlog abandoned. The fix is one step further in the same direction the implementer has already taken - the server reports one violation per refused message, so the record should keep them per subject in arrival order. Separately, and not a failure: the code fix of this round, commit 9e0e2ec5ad0f, carries legion-reviewer[bot] as its author, because it was committed onto the working-copy commit this tester left behind rather than onto a fresh one. The history attributes the implementer's code to the review App. No product, scope or design decision is open.
